body: The end of a relationship is a real loss. You are allowed to treat it as one.
It hurts because it mattered. Nothing about your sadness is silly or too much.
You don't need to understand everything that happened yet. Today, getting through is enough.
Missing someone who was not right for you is still missing someone. Both can be true.
Mornings can be the hardest, when you remember again. Go slowly with yourself.
There is no deadline for being over it. Your pace is the right pace.
Reaching for your phone out of habit is normal. Habits take longer to end than relationships.
Whoever ended it, the hurt is real on your side. You do not have to rank it.
Crying over this is not a step back. It is your heart catching up with the news.
Some days you may feel relief, and other days regret. Neither one cancels the other.
Their side of the bed, their mug, their shows. Small things can hurt the most, and that is normal.
Feeling lost without the daily routine you shared makes sense. A shape has gone from your days.
Anger, sadness, numbness, hope: they can all arrive in one afternoon. Let them pass through.
You are not hard to love. One ending does not get to decide that.
Not wanting to hear advice right now is fine. You can simply say you are not ready to talk.
Looking at old photos is not a failure. Neither is hiding them for a while.
Being alone tonight may feel sharp. It is a feeling passing through, not a verdict on your life.
Wondering what you could have done differently is natural. Try not to stand trial over it every night.
Plans you made together have gone too. Grieving a future is allowed.
Friends may pick sides or go quiet. That is a second hurt, and it deserves kindness too.
If today all you did was get up and eat something, that is a full day in a week like this.
Love that ended was still love. The ending does not make the good parts untrue.
Sleep might be rough for a while. Lying down in the dark and resting still helps your body.
Nobody gets to tell you how long this should take, including the stern voice in your own head.
Wanting to send a message is not the same as needing to send it. The wish alone is allowed.
This kind of tired is real. Heartache uses energy even when you do nothing.
Seeing them move on, or imagining it, can sting badly. It says nothing about your worth.
Quiet evenings can feel very long now. It is fine to fill them with easy, comforting things.
Parts of you may still hope. Hope does not make you foolish, it makes you someone who cared.
A month of this is hard going. You are still here, and that matters.
Start with water this morning. A glass before coffee is a small kindness to yourself.
Open the curtains and a window, even for five minutes. Let the room know it is a new day.
Text one friend today. It does not need to be about the break-up.
Change the sheets if you have the energy. Fresh bedding can make tonight a little easier.
Try ten minutes outside with no headphones. Just you and whatever the street is doing.
Cook or buy one meal you actually like, not one you used to share. Your taste counts.
Consider muting their profile for now. It is not forever, it is just room to breathe.
Put your phone in another room for one hour this evening. See how the hour feels.
Move one piece of furniture or one picture. The space can start to be yours again.
Write down what you want to say to them, then keep the page. It does not need sending.
Take a different route today, to work or the shop. New streets carry fewer memories.
One small plan for the weekend is enough. A coffee, a film, a walk with someone easy.
Steady is the goal this week, not happy. Regular meals and regular sleep do quiet work.
Say yes to one invitation, even if you only stay an hour. Leaving early is always allowed.
Tidy one drawer or one shelf today. A small ordered corner is something to rest your eyes on.
Make a short list of songs that have nothing to do with them. Play it while you wash up.
Stretch for two minutes when you wake. Your body has been holding this too.
Call someone who knew you before the relationship. They remember parts of you that are still here.
Pick up one old hobby for fifteen minutes. You do not have to be good at it today.
Eat breakfast, even something small. Hard mornings are harder on an empty stomach.
When the urge to check their page comes, try waiting ten minutes first. Often it eases a little.
Give this evening a simple shape: food, a wash, one episode, bed. Simple is steadying.
Go to bed at the same time tonight as last night. Rhythm helps when feelings do not.
Buy yourself one small ordinary thing, like fruit or flowers. You are worth looking after.
Sit in a café or a library for a while. Being near other people counts, even without talking.
Let a friend know which days are hardest. People often want to help and do not know when.
Walk until you have noticed five things you had not seen before. Then go home if you like.
Clean your space a little at a time. Ten minutes with a cloth is enough for today.
Tonight, write one line about something that was fine today. Fine is a good word right now.
Drink something warm and sit by a window. Watching the weather is a fair use of ten minutes.
Keep one evening this week only for yourself. Choose the food, the film, the bedtime.
If you slipped and sent a message or looked at photos, be gentle. Tomorrow you can begin again.
Small habits are building under you, even when you cannot feel them. Keep the easy ones going.
Ask one person how their week is. Listening to someone else can rest a busy mind.
Two months of mornings without them, and you have met every one. That takes real steadiness.
Look back at week one for a moment. You are carrying this differently now, even if it still aches.
Early on, an hour without thinking of them felt impossible. Those hours have started to appear.
Whole parts of your day belong only to you again. Notice which ones you like.
Maybe their name stings a little less than it did. If it does not yet, that is fine too.
Your routines are your own now. You built them on some very hard days.
Remember how heavy the first weekend was. You have come through many weekends since.
Somewhere in these weeks you made choices just for you. That is a skill worth keeping.
What you learned about your needs is not wasted. It will travel with you.
Good memories can stay good. You do not have to throw them out to move forward.
Hard evenings may still come. You now know a few things that help you through them.
By now you have proof that you can sit with strong feelings and still get up the next day.
The person you are becoming has been shaped by how gently you treated yourself here.
Think about one thing you would like in the next few months. Small is fine. So is vague.
Friends who stayed close through this are worth thanking. A short message would do.
Space is opening up in your life. There is no rush to fill it with anything.
Trusting again can wait until it feels safe. Wanting to, one day, is already a good sign.
Notice what you do now without thinking of them at all. That list is quietly growing.
One relationship ended. Your ability to care, laugh and connect did not end with it.
Many weeks ago, eating and sleeping were the whole job. See how much more you manage now.
Loneliness may still knock some nights. It no longer gets to rearrange the whole house.
Future you may remember this as the season you kept going. It was not easy, and you did it.
Keep the habits that held you up. Water, walks and early nights are good companions.
Almost three months on, you have a life with your own shape. Still tender in places, and yours.
Forgiving them, or yourself, can come in its own time. It is not a task with a date on it.
These daily notes are nearly finished. The kindness you have practised does not finish with them.
Tomorrow brings the last message. Thank you for reading on the days it was hard to.
Three months have passed since this began. Walk on at your own pace, with your whole heart still yours.
